title: Arise, Lord: the Virgin is the ark

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 13, cols. C-D (PDF p. 37)

source_text: Adeste igitur, vos quoque carissimi, et dulcia verba illa ex spiritali David cithara nobis repraesentata decantemus, dicentes: Surge Domine, in requiem tuam: tu, et arca sanctificationis tuae. Vere enim arca est sanctissima Virgo; intrinsecus et extrinsecus deaurata, quae universum sanctificationis thesaurum suscepit. Surge Domine, in requiem tuam. Surge Domine, ex sinu Patris, ut collapsum primi parentis genus erigas.
pass_a_gloss: Be present/come (adeste) therefore, you also dearest, and those sweet words (dulcia verba) from the spiritual (spiritalis) harp (cithara) of David represented (repraesentata) to us let us sing (decantemus), saying: Arise (surge) Lord, into your rest (requies): you, and the ark of your sanctification (arca sanctificationis). For truly an ark (arca) is the most holy Virgin; within and without (intrinsecus et extrinsecus) gilded (deaurata), which received (suscepit) the whole treasure of sanctification. Arise Lord, into your rest. Arise Lord, from the bosom of the Father (ex sinu Patris), that you may raise (erigas) the fallen (collapsum) race (genus) of the first parent (primus parens).

choices.choice: 'intrinsecus et extrinsecus deaurata' alludes to the ark overlaid with gold inside and out (Exodus 25:11); cited.
'ex sinu Patris' takes its phrase from John 1:18; cited. sanctificatio rendered 'holiness', as in section 8.

pass_b_english: Come then, you too, beloved, and let us sing those sweet words set before us from the spiritual harp of David, saying: Arise, O Lord, into Your resting place, You and the ark of Your holiness (Psalm 132:8). For truly the most holy Virgin is an ark, gilded within and without (Exodus 25:11), who received the whole treasure of holiness. Arise, O Lord, into Your resting place (Psalm 132:8). Arise, O Lord, from the bosom of the Father (John 1:18), to raise up the fallen race of the first parent.
notes: Margin 'Psal. 131' is Vulgate numbering: Vulgate Psalm 131:8 = Psalm 132:8 in English Bibles; English numbering cited. The Latin 'arca sanctificationis tuae' is translated from the sermon's text ('ark of Your holiness'), not from the Hebrew-based English ('ark of Your might'). 'intrinsecus et extrinsecus deaurata' alludes to the ark overlaid with gold inside and out (Exodus 25:11); cited. 'ex sinu Patris' takes its phrase from John 1:18; cited. sanctificatio rendered 'holiness', as in section 8.
